topic: How can frequency planning address interference between satellite uplinks and broadband power line communication systems?
consensus_response: Frequency planning can address interference by separating frequency bands, using orthogonal polarizations, and implementing exclusion zones. Adaptive frequency allocation and machine learning integration can dynamically adjust frequencies to minimize interference. Edge computing enhances real-time decision-making, while beamforming techniques direct signals to specific areas, reducing interference and improving SINR.
reference_context: Satellite and terrestrial networks operating on the same frequency band can cause interference, particularly in uplink scenarios, highlighting the need for careful frequency planning and separation.
